newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 21.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 21.

text.p: ------------------------- WAM ------------------------ ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST..... ------------------- July 21, 1997------------------ Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends *********************************************** ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
CHICAGO - Telecommunications company Ameritech Corp appoints Ammirati Puris Lintas to handle its $100 million consumer, business and brand advertising accounts. *********

FRANKFURT - Coca-Cola's German unit awards its main advertising account to agency Michael Conrad & Leo Burnett. Publicis International, which won the beverage giant's European account two years ago, will continue to represent the company's brand name internationally, a Coca-Cola GmbH spokesman says. *********
SACRAMENTO, California - California's Senate votes to ban cigarette advertising on billboards near schools and playgrounds, in an effort to reduce smoking among children. *********

LONDON - An advertising campaign for condoms in Lebanon has done away with traditional safe sex warnings in favour of a message about sensuality, London International Group Plc, maker of Durex condoms, says. *********

MUNICH - Developing local, advertising-financed television in Germany remains difficult, says Thomas Kirch, the media investor and son of television and film mogul Leo Kirch. He tells CineChart, the ProSieben Media AG in-house newsletter, "There still aren't any real local TV advertising markets that have developed (in Germany). The production of local TV advertising is still too costly." Thomas Kirch is a majority shareholder in ProSieben Media AG. *********

NEW YORK - Wells Rich Greene BDDP ad agency says it is changing its name to Wells BDDP. The company is a unit of Paris-based BDDP Worldwide. "We are changing our name to reinforce our global identity and the fact that we are very much a part of the BDDP worldwide network," says a spokesman. *********

HAMBURG - Private television station Super RTL hands its ad account to Start Advertising, a Munich-based agency, industry news service Text Intern reports. DDB in Dusseldorf previously held the account. *********
CHICAGO - Kraft Foods appoints WPP Group's J. Walter Thompson USA, Chicago, to explore options for promoting the food giant's brands under one corporate umbrella. *********

HAMBURG - The advertising income of private German TV stations increased in the first half of 1997 at a higher rate than that of all other media, publishing house Gruner + Jahr Verlag says, based on data provided by ad research firm Nielsen S + P. Private channels boosted gross income 10.5 percent to 5.3 billion marks ($3 billion). Taken together, print media, television and radio ad income climbed four percent to 13.0 billion marks. *********

NEW YORK - Software watch dog group, the Business Software Alliance, says it is launching a campaign to battle software piracy in the advertising industry. *********************************************** MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

REDWOOD CITY, California - Excite Inc. says it plans to offer free Web-based e-mail in conjunction with an undisclosed e-mail company. The agreement will make Excite the first Internet search company to offer free e-mail. *********

DUBAI - Arab satellite operator Arabsat says it stopped its transmissions of French channel Canal France International (CFI), saying it had shown a pornographic film and violated Islamic views of decency. It says it canncelled its contract with CFI. *********

AMSTERDAM - Philips Electronics NV says it will gradually wind down its media activities, but will leave its PolyGram stake untouched. Chairman Cor Boonstra says that the Dutch electronics giant is ill-equipped for the fast-moving media sector. *********

LONDON - A blast from the past, Radio London comes back on the air 30 years after the pirate rock music station was forced to stop broadcasting from a ship in the North Sea. To mark the anniversary broadcasts have been resumed for 28 days, although this time the station has a licence from Britain's Radio Authority. *********

PASADENA, California - NBC television network says that its refusal to join the new U.S. television ratings system is not prompted by a fear of losing ad dollars but by worries over censorship. *********

PARIS - France Television, which groups the two general French public television stations, has asked the government for 150 million francs ($24.8 million) extra next year, newspapers report. *********************************************** BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
HARARE- Soft drinks giant Coca-Cola is driving deep into Africa in an investment expansion expected to draw other U.S. companies along, according to industry observers. *********

SHANGHAI - The number of Chinese families buying personal computers for home use will swell over the next several years until the computer rivals other common household appliances, an Intel Corp executive says. *********
MOSCOW - UK confectioner Cadbury Schweppes Plc officially opens a chocolate plant near St Petersburg in Russia, its biggest such project outside Britain. *********

SAN JOSE, Costa Rica - Tiny Costa Rica plans to demand millions of dollars in compensation from big tobacco companies for the cost of treating smoking-related diseases, an official says. ********* PARIS - The founders of Club Med quit in a dispute over the direction of the French resort chain, which reported a big loss for the first half of its fiscal year. *********

PARIS - Orangina says it is revamping the image of its recently-acquired Ricqles brand to put more sparkle in the minty soda. The revamp includes more modern packaging and a television advertising campaign. *********
FRANKFURT - German carmaker BMW AG expects to make a seven percent pre-tax return on sales within the next 10 years, BMW chief executive Bernd Pischetsrieder says. *********

BELGRADE - Serbian privatisation minister Milan Beko met representatives of the French tobacco company Seita, which appears interested in investing in Yugoslavia's tobacco industry, the Information Ministry says. *********************************************** CONSUMER TRENDS:
SYDNEY - Australian consumers are switching their spending from shops to restaurants and cinemas, a survey by advertising agency George Patterson Bates says. *********

DURRES, Albania - After trying to keep foreigners out of the country for 40 years, Albania is now desperately trying to get them in and gain a share of the international holiday market, say government officials. *********

BEIJING - China has told its millions of laid off workers to go out and find new jobs and not wait for the state to find work for them. They also need to lower their lofty expectations if they wanted to find employment, the official Workers' Daily says. *********
DUBLIN - Ireland's pigeon-racing fraternity have their feathers ruffled. Their birds are going missing, and they suspect mobile phones may be disrupting their homing instincts. *********

STUTTGART - The number of jobless in Germany could be halved by the year 2002 if the country's labour market becomes more flexible, the President of the German Labour Office says. Bernhard Jagoda said that certain conditions aimed at introducing more flexibity into Germany's rigid employment structures need to be met if jobless numbers are to be cut. *********************************************** -- London Advertising Newsdesk +44 171 542 2792 *********************************************** See full stories on Reuters Advertising & Media Briefing.
